newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coalition parties meet at Kohl's office.
newsitem.headline: German coalition parties meet at Kohl's office.

text.p: Leaders from the German government's coalition parties met for 90 minutes early on Tuesday to discuss budgetary problems and their controversial plan to revalue Bundesbank assets.
The leaders of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), the Bavarian sister party CSU and the liberal Free Democrats (FDP) met at Kohl's office for the second time in three days.
There was no immediate details available about the meeting.

Media accounts of a similar meeting on Sunday said that Finance Minister Theo Waigel wants to raise petrol taxes or delay the reduction in the 7.5 percent solidary income tax surcharge to fill the budget holes.
The FDP says it is strictly opposed to tax increases.
The finance ministry says that there is a hole in the 1997 budget of up to 30 billion marks ($17.4 billion) -- due to tax revenue shortfalls and higher than expected unemployment this year.
